findings: Full event catering (50-100 people, '$800-$1500') was NEVER asked about. Birdie only asked 'your tiffin pricing... and roughly what areas you deliver to' and later addressed party trays only when Priya herself raised it at the very end ('the party trays, I don't think we talked about those'). The brief has zero mention of event catering pricing at all — a core service line is completely missing from services_and_pricing.

Party tray pricing ($120-160) was never captured as a number; Birdie just agreed it falls in the 'no pricing, follow up' bucket without ever eliciting the range, unlike tiffin pricing which was captured with numbers.

Hours of operation were never asked about at all (tiffin pickup/delivery Mon-Fri 11am-1pm & 6-8pm, weekend catering by request). This is a basic operational fact a WhatsApp bot would need to answer 'are you open now' type questions, and it's entirely absent from the brief.

Business background — home-based Fremont CA location, cottage food operation permit, 6 years in business, growth from tiffin to event catering — was never asked. 'business_description' field in the final brief is explicitly null despite Priya volunteering her business name upfront.

Staff/team structure (Priya cooks alone; niece Anjali helps packing/delivery weekends only, no fixed schedule) was only mentioned in passing re: delivery fees ('if Anjali's free that day to drive') and never explored or captured as a structured fact — no staffing info appears anywhere in the brief.

Subscriber count uncertainty ('25, or maybe 30') and Priya's stated pain point of undercharging/not knowing her margins were never surfaced by Birdie, despite being a core anxiety area from the fact sheet that a chatbot project might reasonably want to know about (e.g., for the 'success criteria' or 'pain points' framing).

Cancellation/refund policy for tiffin subscriptions ('should be a day before but I'm flexible', 'no official refund policy... usually just works it out') was never asked; the brief only captures the catering deposit gap, not the tiffin-side flexibility policy at all.

Evidence-gathering was attempted once ('do you have any real WhatsApp chats or screenshots') but was dropped immediately when Priya said she wasn't sure how to upload — no follow-up attempt to get her to paste text examples directly in the chat, which would have been low-effort and higher-fidelity than relying on her paraphrased 3 example questions.

The final brief's 'open_items' list absorbs several core facts that should arguably be resolved data points, not follow-ups — e.g., party tray range and event catering range should have simply been asked rather than left as 'need to decide how bot should quote a range.'
top_improvement: Systematically walk through EVERY service tier mentioned in the business (tiffin, party trays, full event catering, delivery) with an explicit price-range question for each, instead of asking broadly about 'tiffin pricing and delivery areas' and letting bigger-ticket items (event catering) fall through entirely.
schema_suggestions: Add a dedicated 'business_background' or 'business_context' field (location, licensing/permit status, years in operation, how the business has grown) — currently business_description is null with no mechanism forcing Birdie to ask basic background questions.
Add an explicit 'hours_of_operation' field to the schema — there is currently no slot for this at all, which is why it was never asked despite being fundamental to a customer-facing bot.
Add a 'staff_or_team' field to capture who does what (owner-operated vs. helpers, schedules) — currently this information has nowhere to live and gets dropped even when mentioned in passing (Anjali).

Add a 'services_and_pricing' completeness check/field that requires listing ALL service tiers with a range or 'unknown/varies' flag per tier, rather than a free-text list that can silently omit an entire tier (event catering was fully dropped).

Add a 'known_pain_points' or 'owner_concerns' field distinct from 'open_items' — currently pain points like undercharging, subscriber count uncertainty, and hiring anxiety have no home and were simply never elicited, likely because there's no schema slot prompting the interviewer to ask 'what's frustrating you about the business side of things.'

The 'additional_notes' and 'open_items' fields are being used as a catch-all for scope decisions and policy gaps (e.g., deposit policy, calendar tool) — consider a structured 'unresolved_decisions' field so these aren't mixed in with generic notes and follow-up reminders.
